task: Authenticate via company SSO
story: As a CS Agent, I want to sign in to the portal using my company SSO, so that I don't need yet another password and IT keeps me in their identity system
outcome: I don't need yet another password and IT keeps me in their identity system
reasoning: Foundational: nothing else ships without auth. SSO is mandatory for fintech internal tool.

task: Authenticate via company SSO
story: As a CS Agent, I want to be auto-signed-out after a period of inactivity, so that an unattended laptop can't be used to issue refunds
outcome: an unattended laptop can't be used to issue refunds
reasoning: Compliance-mandated for money-movement tooling. Small additional work once SSO is wired.

task: Authenticate via company SSO
story: As a CS Agent, I want SSO to remember me across browser sessions within the working day, so that I'm not re-authenticating every time I open the portal
outcome: I'm not re-authenticating every time I open the portal
reasoning: Quality of life; sleeps fine until pilot users complain.

task: Get the right access scope for my role
story: As a CS Agent, I want to land on a page scoped to refund actions only, so that I can't accidentally wander into admin tooling
outcome: I can't accidentally wander into admin tooling
reasoning: RBAC is required; this is the UI side of it. Cheap once SSO roles exist.

task: Get the right access scope for my role
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to see a "pending approvals" entry point in addition to issuing my own refunds, so that I know what's waiting on me
outcome: I know what's waiting on me
reasoning: Required for the approval workflow to actually work end-to-end in pi-1.

task: Get the right access scope for my role
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to view the list of CS Agents currently provisioned and their last-active time, so that I can spot stale or unused accounts during quarterly reviews
outcome: I can spot stale or unused accounts during quarterly reviews
reasoning: Compliance-flavored hygiene, but quarterly cadence means it can wait.

task: Get the right access scope for my role
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to grant/revoke a CS Agent's refund capability from within the portal, so that I don't have to file an IT ticket every time we onboard or offboard someone
outcome: I don't have to file an IT ticket every time we onboard or offboard someone
reasoning: Convenience for the lead; IT ticket path works fine for the volumes involved (~5-15 agents).

task: Look up by customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want to search for a customer by email address, so that I can start from how the customer identifies themselves to me
outcome: I can start from how the customer identifies themselves to me
reasoning: Primary entry point for ~80%+ of refund cases per H1. Without it, no MVP.

task: Look up by customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want to see the customer's recent transactions (last 90 days) listed newest-first, so that I can pick the right one without knowing the transaction ID
outcome: I can pick the right one without knowing the transaction ID
reasoning: Direct payoff of H1; lets agents work the way they think.

task: Look up by customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want to filter the transaction list by date range or amount, so that I can find the right one when the customer says "the $42 charge from a couple weeks ago"
outcome: I can find the right one when the customer says "the $42 charge from a couple weeks ago"
reasoning: Improves agent speed once base lookup is in place; not a slice-1 blocker.

task: Look up by customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want to search by customer ID or account ID in addition to email, so that I can still find them when the customer reaches out from a different email
outcome: I can still find them when the customer reaches out from a different email
reasoning: Edge case; email covers most of H1's 80%+ target.

task: Look up by transaction ID directly
story: As a CS Agent, I want to paste a transaction ID into a single search box and jump straight to that transaction, so that escalations that already have an ID don't need a multi-step lookup
outcome: escalations that already have an ID don't need a multi-step lookup
reasoning: Cheap to add once the lookup endpoint exists; covers the engineering-handoff flow.

task: Handle "no results"
story: As a CS Agent, I want a clear "not found" message when a customer email doesn't match anything, so that I don't waste time wondering whether the lookup is broken or the customer is wrong
outcome: I don't waste time wondering whether the lookup is broken or the customer is wrong
reasoning: Cheap empty-state polish that prevents support churn against the new tool.

task: Handle "no results"
story: As a CS Agent, I want suggestions when my search has a near-miss (typo, alternate email domain), so that I can recover from common input errors
outcome: I can recover from common input errors
reasoning: Nice; not load-bearing.

task: See the transaction in context
story: As a CS Agent, I want to see transaction details (amount, date, customer, payment method last 4, original currency, current refund status), so that I have the facts I need to decide
outcome: I have the facts I need to decide
reasoning: Without this the agent can't confidently refund. Mostly read endpoint + render.

task: See the transaction in context
story: As a CS Agent, I want to see prior refunds against this same transaction (if any), so that I don't accidentally issue a duplicate refund
outcome: I don't accidentally issue a duplicate refund
reasoning: Duplicate-refund prevention is the #1 finance risk of self-service. Mandatory.

task: See the transaction in context
story: As a CS Agent, I want to see this customer's refund history across all their transactions, so that I can spot a pattern (frequent refunder) before issuing another
outcome: I can spot a pattern (frequent refunder) before issuing another
reasoning: Helps catch abuse; secondary control once duplicate-on-txn is covered.

task: Understand whether I'm allowed to refund this
story: As a CS Agent, I want the portal to tell me explicitly whether this transaction is refundable (eligible / not eligible / needs lead approval) before I try, so that I'm not surprised at the submit step
outcome: I'm not surprised at the submit step
reasoning: Eligibility gate is the heart of self-service trust. Drives both H2 and H4.

task: Understand whether I'm allowed to refund this
story: As a CS Agent, I want a clear reason when a transaction is not refundable via the portal (e.g., "partial refund — escalate to engineering", "settled batch — escalate"), so that I know exactly what to do next
outcome: I know exactly what to do next
reasoning: Defines the escalation path back to eng cleanly; tied to non-goals.

task: Understand whether I'm allowed to refund this
story: As a CS Agent, I want the eligibility rules and approval thresholds to be visible/explainable in the UI, so that I can answer a customer's "why" without guessing
outcome: I can answer a customer's "why" without guessing
reasoning: Helps customer comms; secondary to actually having the rules enforced.

task: Submit a refund within my limit
story: As a CS Agent, I want to click a single "Refund" button for an eligible transaction within my limit, so that the common case is one click
outcome: the common case is one click
reasoning: The core action. Everything else exists to enable this happening cleanly.

task: Submit a refund within my limit
story: As a CS Agent, I want to enter a short reason code + free-text note before submitting, so that finance and my Lead can understand why later
outcome: finance and my Lead can understand why later
reasoning: Required for the audit trail finance signs off on (H4).

task: Submit a refund within my limit
story: As a CS Agent, I want a confirm step ("Refund $X to <customer>?") before the action is final, so that I can catch wrong-transaction mistakes before they happen
outcome: I can catch wrong-transaction mistakes before they happen
reasoning: Mistake-prevention is critical when refunds are real money. Tiny code cost.

task: Submit a refund within my limit
story: As a CS Agent, I want the submit action to be idempotent if I double-click, so that a flaky network doesn't cause a duplicate refund
outcome: a flaky network doesn't cause a duplicate refund
reasoning: Should be pi-1, but the payments API may already enforce idempotency keys — confirm in week 1. Promoting if confirmed.

task: Send a refund above my limit for approval
story: As a CS Agent, I want to submit a refund-with-approval-request when the amount is above my limit, so that I'm not blocked from handling the case at all
outcome: I'm not blocked from handling the case at all
reasoning: Required to make the "don't-need-engineering" outcome real for higher-value refunds.

task: Send a refund above my limit for approval
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to see a list of pending refund approvals with all the context the agent provided, so that I can approve or deny in one screen
outcome: I can approve or deny in one screen
reasoning: The Lead's primary surface. Paired with S025 to close the loop.

task: Send a refund above my limit for approval
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to approve or deny with a required short reason, so that there's a record of why
outcome: there's a record of why
reasoning: Audit-required (H4). Trivial UI on top of S026.

task: Send a refund above my limit for approval
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want to be notified (email + in-portal) when a new approval is waiting, so that customers aren't waiting on me without my knowing
outcome: customers aren't waiting on me without my knowing
reasoning: Pi-1 will rely on Lead checking the queue manually; notification is an obvious next step.

task: Send a refund above my limit for approval
story: As a CS Agent, I want to see the status of my pending approval requests (waiting / approved / denied), so that I can update the customer without nagging my Lead
outcome: I can update the customer without nagging my Lead
reasoning: Workflow polish; agents can ask in Slack at pi-1.

task: Handle failures from the payments service
story: As a CS Agent, I want a clear human-readable error message if the payments service rejects the refund (with a "copy details for engineering" button), so that I have a clean escalation path
outcome: I have a clean escalation path
reasoning: Without this, every payments-API error becomes an angry Slack ping back at eng — defeats the purpose.

task: Handle failures from the payments service
story: As a CS Agent, I want the portal to auto-retry transient payments-service failures (with backoff) before showing me an error, so that I'm not bothered by blips
outcome: I'm not bothered by blips
reasoning: Pi-1 surfaces the error; pi-2 reduces the noise floor.

task: See that the refund actually happened
story: As a CS Agent, I want a clear "Refund complete" confirmation screen with the refund ID and timestamp, so that I know I can close the customer ticket
outcome: I know I can close the customer ticket
reasoning: Closes the loop; without it, agents will double-check in another tool.

task: See that the refund actually happened
story: As a CS Agent, I want the original transaction row to update to show "Refunded" immediately after, so that I'm not left guessing if I refresh
outcome: I'm not left guessing if I refresh
reasoning: State-consistency basic; user trust killer if missing.

task: Communicate to the customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want a copyable confirmation snippet (refund amount, expected funds-availability window, refund ID) to paste into our CS-tool reply, so that customer messaging is consistent and complete
outcome: customer messaging is consistent and complete
reasoning: Single biggest time-save inside CS's own workflow. Tiny build cost.

task: Communicate to the customer
story: As a CS Agent, I want the portal to send a transactional refund-confirmation email to the customer on my behalf, so that I don't have to copy-paste anything
outcome: I don't have to copy-paste anything
reasoning: Crosses a real org boundary (transactional email infra, brand voice review). Defer.

task: Leave a trail for finance and audit
story: As a system, log every refund attempt (success and failure) with: who, when, txn ID, amount, reason code, free-text note, approval chain
reasoning: Non-negotiable for fintech. Drives H4. Built-in from day 1 or the project loses finance's blessing.

task: Leave a trail for finance and audit
story: As a Finance analyst, I want to export the refund audit log as CSV for a given date range, so that I can reconcile against the payments processor at month-end
outcome: I can reconcile against the payments processor at month-end
reasoning: Finance needs this for first month-end after pilot; CSV is the lowest-friction format.

task: Leave a trail for finance and audit
story: As a CS Team Lead, I want a per-agent refund summary (count, total amount, denied/approved breakdown) for the last 30 days, so that I can spot outliers in my team's behavior
outcome: I can spot outliers in my team's behavior
reasoning: Lead-visibility win; not load-bearing for pi-1.

task: Leave a trail for finance and audit
story: As a Finance analyst, I want the audit-log export to include a stable refund-ID that matches the payments processor's record, so that reconciliation is unambiguous
outcome: reconciliation is unambiguous
reasoning: Reconciliation pain killer; tightly coupled to the payments processor's ID model.

task: Identity, access, and audit-trail integrity
story: Wire portal authentication to company SSO with `cs-agent` and `cs-lead` roles provisioned in the identity provider
reasoning: Foundational, blocks every user story. Paired with S001.

task: Identity, access, and audit-trail integrity
story: All refund actions require an authenticated session; backend rejects anything else
reasoning: Non-negotiable security control; one of the things a fintech audit will ask about first.

task: Identity, access, and audit-trail integrity
story: Audit log is append-only and stored separately from the application DB (or on storage with retention/legal-hold)
reasoning: Required for SOC 2 / PCI-tone compliance and for H4 sign-off. Real infra work.

task: Identity, access, and audit-trail integrity
story: Pen-test pass against the portal before scaling beyond pilot CS agents
reasoning: Gates pi-3 widening of access; doesn't gate pilot. Costly externally-driven work.

task: Operability baseline

task: Operability baseline

reasoning: Doc + small UI affordance; pi-1 can ship without and surface raw errors.

reasoning: Trust-multiplier for the deploy pipeline; pi-1 can rely on manual smoke for first month.

reasoning: Free outcome multiplier; cost is one PM-day.

task: Get CS productive with the portal
story: In-app first-run tour for new CS Agents
reasoning: Useful once team grows beyond initial pilot.
